skills.name: auto_research-stage-1-skill
skills.description: V3.2 deep-research opportunity mapping with enforced full-text depth, citation chaining, synthesis, persistent checkpoints, and independent acceptance.

skills.name: auto_research-stage-2-skill
skills.description: V3.2 top-conference idea development with mode-aware paper realization, capability-qualified experimental design, deep collision audits, discriminative pilots, reviewer-guided improvement, and independent acceptance.

skills.name: auto_research-stage-3-skill
skills.description: V3.2 top-conference full-scale validation with capability-qualified design, preregistered claim-complete experiments, persistent run tracking, hourly health reconciliation, throughput-qualified CPU/GPU utilization, statistical adequacy, and independent acceptance.

skills.name: auto_research-stage-4-skill
skills.description: V1.0 evidence-grounded paper writing from a validated Stage 3 handoff, with official venue resources, durable paper packages, and at least three rounds of independent writing and visual-format review before Stage 5 handoff.

skills.name: auto_research-stage-5-skill
skills.description: V1.0 calibrated multi-model technical peer review with evidence adjudication, managed experiment repair, fresh re-review, integrity-preserving result reporting, and submission-readiness gating.

skills.name: idea-spark
skills.description: Generate ONE reviewer-defensible, implementable research idea with a concrete method and falsification plan from a stated research direction. Use when the user asks for a research idea, novelty analysis, bottleneck diagnosis, or paper-shape suggestion. Skip code review, debugging, and unconstrained brainstorming without research context.

skills.name: paper-search
skills.description: Search papers across arXiv, DBLP, OpenAlex, OpenReview, Semantic Scholar, and Crossref for a given query and year range, using ./scripts/search_papers.py. Use when the user asks to find papers, related work, prior art, or recent publications on a specific topic, especially when they mention a date range or specific venues like NeurIPS, ICLR, or ICML.

skills.name: paper2blog
skills.description: Use when transforming an academic paper, arXiv/OpenReview PDF, conference paper, technical report, poster, slide deck, repository README, or related research materials into a bilingual editorial package for an editing team. Produces two articles by default — a Chinese WeChat public-account version (`blog_zh.docx`) and an English research-blog version (`blog_en.docx`). Use for drafting, revising, or packaging article copy, figure placement, captions, image prompts, and the final `.docx` deliverables.

skills.name: paper2poster
skills.description: Render a pre-extracted paper's structured 9-section spec (`paper_spec.md`) into a single-page HTML academic poster, fit the layout to the page via an iterative measured-fill loop, and export it to print-ready PDF + PNG thumbnail. Requires the upstream `paper2assets` skill to have produced the input `<outdir>/` package (`manifest.json` at the root + an `assets/` folder holding `meta/paper_spec.md`, `meta/text.txt`, `meta/figures.json`, `meta/metadata.json`, `figures/*.png`, `logos/`, `qr/`) first. Use when the user wants an HTML poster, PDF/PNG export, or PPTX from a paper they already have extracted assets for — e.g., "render the poster", "make the poster from this spec", "export poster to PDF", "paper2poster". The three skills paper2assets → paper2poster → html2pptx run in sequence, each invokable on its own.

skills.name: paper2reel
skills.description: Build an interactive HTML viewer that aligns paper2poster output with slide/video deck frames through a sidecar content_alignment.json, without modifying the original poster, PPTX, or blog deliverables.

skills.name: paper2video
skills.description: Turn a research paper, a paper2assets package, or an existing PPT deck into a narrated MP4 video. Prefer the shared paper2assets package when present so paper2poster, paper2blog, paper2slides, and paper2video use the same section order and narration. Preserve the advanced deck route by delegating slide authoring to the external `hugohe3/ppt-master` project, then synthesize audio with `skills/paper2poster/scripts/generate_audio.py`, render with `skills/paper2video/scripts/render_video.py`, and burn final subtitles with `skills/paper2video/scripts/add_subtitles.py`.

skills.name: research-workspace-manager
skills.description: Single entry point for research on the xasi-agent-training VM: load storage context, reuse existing assets, and enforce Project→Idea→Attempt→Run workspace organization. Use at the start of any local research task, experiment, model/dataset/paper download, new idea, retry, run, or archive operation.

skills.name: scoop-check
skills.description: Check whether a proposed research novelty (given a problem statement and claimed idea/novelty) overlaps with existing published work. TRIGGER when the user asks to verify research novelty, check if an idea is new, compare a proposed contribution to prior art, do a literature/prior-art search for a specific claim, or assess whether a paper idea has been scooped. DO NOT TRIGGER for general literature reviews unrelated to a specific novelty claim, or for writing related-work sections of an already-validated idea.

skills.name: stage-1-skill
skills.description: Local-first opportunity mapping for agentic RL table research directions with manager-backed evidence handoff.

skills.name: stage-2-skill
skills.description: Convert a Stage 1 direction into bounded, audited Stage 2 idea support with manager-safe lifecycle tracking.

skills.name: stage-3-skill
skills.description: Execute an approved full-scale validation attempt from a Stage 2 handoff with preregistration, audits, and claim-safe reporting.

skills.name: customize-cloud-agent
skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

skills.name: github-pr-media
skills.description: Upload an image or video to GitHub's user attachments API and embed it in a pull request description or comment. Use when asked to add screenshots, diagrams, recordings, or other media to a PR or GitHub comment.

3. You are given one continuous FlightGear cockpit recording at
4. `/workspace/materials/flight.mp4`. Spoken air-traffic-control clearances are on
5. the audio track. The visible analog instruments show how the aircraft responds.
6.

8. aircraft's subsequent visible behavior.
9. 
10. The recording contains five independent 12-minute flight legs joined by visible
11. hard cuts at 720, 1440, 2160, and 2880 seconds. Aircraft state and open
12. clearances reset at each cut. Supersession and stable-hold windows never cross a
13. leg boundary. An unfinished clearance at the end of its leg is `incomplete`
14. unless it is otherwise `violated`.
15. 
16. An offline speech-to-text tool is installed:
17. 
18. ```bash
19. transcribe /workspace/materials/flight.mp4
20. transcribe /workspace/materials/flight.mp4 --start 600 --end 900
21. ```
22. 
23. It prints timestamped speech segments but no aircraft-state information.
24. `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` are available for extracting audio, clips, and frames.
25. 
26. ## Instrument layout
27. 
28. The standard six-pack is visible on the left side of the panel:
29. 
30. - airspeed indicator: upper-left round gauge;
31. - altimeter: upper-right round gauge;
32. - heading indicator: lower-center round compass card;
33. - vertical-speed indicator: lower-right round gauge.
34. 
35. The recording contains no selected-heading, selected-altitude, or selected-speed
36. display. Command targets come from the spoken audio; outcomes come from the
37. visible instruments.
38. 
39. ## Clearance fields
40. 
41. For each clearance report exactly:
42. 
43. - `clearance_index`: one-based chronological index.
44. - `issued_time_s`: when the controller begins speaking the clearance, in seconds
45.   from the start of the video.
46. - `command_type`: one value from the closed vocabulary below.
47. - `target_value`: the spoken numeric target.
48. - `target_unit`: `feet`, `degrees`, or `knots`.
49. - `issue_altitude_ft`, `issue_heading_deg`, `issue_airspeed_kt`: the complete
50.   three-instrument state at issue time.
51. - `maximum_commanded_progress`: the greatest nonnegative movement from
52.   the issue-time value in the commanded direction before the next
53.   same-dimension clearance or leg end, in `target_unit`.
54. - `execution_altitude_ft`, `execution_heading_deg`, `execution_airspeed_kt`:
55.   the complete instrument state at `execution_start_time_s`, or all `null` when
56.   execution is `null`.
57. - `completion_altitude_ft`, `completion_heading_deg`,
58.   `completion_airspeed_kt`: the complete instrument state at
59.   `completion_time_s`, or all `null` when completion is `null`.
60. - `ending_altitude_ft`, `ending_heading_deg`, `ending_airspeed_kt`: the complete
61.   three-instrument state immediately before the next same-dimension clearance
62.   or leg end.
63. - `execution_start_time_s`: the first sustained correct-direction response, or
64.   `null`.
65. - `completion_time_s`: the first stable completion time, or `null`.
66. - `status`: one value from the closed vocabulary below.
67. - `superseded_by_index`: the later same-dimension clearance that replaced this
68.   one before completion, or `null`.
69. - `overshoot_bucket`: `none`, `small`, `large`, or `not_applicable`.
70. 
71. Report times to the nearest 0.1 second. Issue times are evaluated within 2
72. seconds; execution and completion times within 4 seconds.
73. 
74. Heading targets use normalized values from 0 through 359 degrees. Target,
75. progress, and every state snapshot are evaluated within 25 feet, 2 degrees, or
76. 2 knots according to their unit. Heading progress uses circular distance in the
77. spoken turn direction.
78. 
79. ## Closed vocabularies
80. 
81. `command_type`:
82. 
83. ```text
84. climb
85. descend
86. turn_left_heading
87. turn_right_heading
88. accelerate
89. decelerate
90. ```
91. 
92. Spoken speed clearances use “maintain N knots.” Classify them as `accelerate`
93. when the pre-clearance airspeed is below N and `decelerate` when it is above N.
94. 
95. `status`:
96. 
97. ```text
98. complied
99. complied_late
100. superseded
101. violated
102. incomplete
103. ```
104. 
105. ## Event definitions
106. 
107. Each clearance belongs to one dimension: altitude, heading, or airspeed. A later
108. clearance supersedes only an unfinished clearance on the same dimension.
109. 
110. `execution_start_time_s` is the first point after issue where the correct trend
111. is sustained for at least 2 seconds:
112. 
113. - heading: at least 0.5 degrees/second in the commanded turn direction;
114. - altitude: at least 100 feet/minute in the commanded direction;
115. - airspeed: at least 0.5 knots/second in the required direction.
116. 
117. `completion_time_s` is the first point after execution from which the indicated
118. value remains within tolerance until the next same-dimension clearance or the
119. end of the video. At least 3 seconds of remaining evidence is required:
120. 
121. - heading: within 8 degrees of target;
122. - altitude: within 100 feet of target;
123. - airspeed: within 3 knots of target.
124. 
125. Apply status precedence in this order:
126. 
127. 1. `complied_late` or `complied` if stable completion occurs. It is
128.    `complied_late` when correct execution begins more than 12 seconds after
129.    issue; otherwise it is `complied`.
130. 2. `superseded` if no stable completion occurs before a later same-dimension
131.    clearance.
132. 3. `violated` if no supersession occurs and a wrong-direction trend meeting the
133.    execution threshold is sustained for at least 2 seconds.
134. 4. `incomplete` otherwise, including when the current flight leg ends.
135. 
136. Overshoot is the maximum excursion beyond the target in the commanded direction
137. before the next same-dimension clearance or leg end:
138. 
139. - heading: `small` when over 8 and at most 15 degrees; `large` when over 15;
140. - altitude: `small` when over 100 and at most 250 feet; `large` when over 250;
141. - airspeed: `small` when over 3 and at most 10 knots; `large` when over 10.
142. 
143. Use `none` when the target is not crossed beyond its tolerance.
144. `not_applicable` is reserved for schema compatibility and is not expected for
145. the directional clearances in this recording.

import cv2, numpy as np, sys

VID = "materials/flight.mp4"

# gauge centers (cx, cy) in original 1280x720 frame, and radii for needle sampling
GAUGES = {
    'asi': dict(cx=523, cy=391, r0=8, r1=40),
    'alt': dict(cx=723, cy=398, r0=6, r1=34),
    'hdg': dict(cx=626, cy=507, r0=10, r1=40),
    'vsi': dict(cx=722, cy=511, r0=8, r1=40),
}

def get_frame(t):
    cap = cv2.VideoCapture(VID)
    cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_MSEC, t*1000.0)
    ok, f = cap.read()
    cap.release()
    if not ok: raise RuntimeError("no frame at %s"%t)
    return f

def radial_profile(gray, cx, cy, r0, r1, nang=720):
    angs = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, nang, endpoint=False)
    rs = np.arange(r0, r1)
    prof = np.zeros(nang)
    for i,a in enumerate(angs):
        xs = (cx + rs*np.cos(a)).astype(int)
        ys = (cy + rs*np.sin(a)).astype(int)
        vals = gray[ys, xs].astype(float)
        prof[i] = vals.mean()
    return angs, prof

def needle_angle(gray, g, nang=720):
    angs, prof = radial_profile(gray, g['cx'], g['cy'], g['r0'], g['r1'], nang)
    # background subtract
    prof = prof - np.median(prof)
    prof[prof<0]=0
    i = int(np.argmax(prof))
    # refine with weighted centroid over a window
    w=8
    idx = [(i+k)%nang for k in range(-w,w+1)]
    wsum = prof[idx]
    a_ref = _circ_centroid(angs[idx], wsum)
    deg = (np.degrees(a_ref))%360
    return deg, prof.max()

def _circ_centroid(angs, weights):
    x=np.sum(weights*np.cos(angs)); y=np.sum(weights*np.sin(angs))
    return np.arctan2(y,x)

if __name__=='__main__':
    t=float(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv)>1 else 30
    f=get_frame(t)
    gray=cv2.cvtColor(f, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    for name,g in GAUGES.items():
        deg,mx=needle_angle(gray,g)
        print(f"{name}: angle={deg:.1f} deg (0=east,CW+ downward since image y down) strength={mx:.1f}")

import cv2, numpy as np, sys, time

VID = "materials/flight.mp4"
FPS = 15.0
SAMPLE_HZ = 2.0
STEP = int(round(FPS/SAMPLE_HZ))  # process every STEP-th frame

GAUGES = {
    'asi': dict(cx=523, cy=391, r0=8, r1=41),
    'alt': dict(cx=723, cy=398, r0=6, r1=35),
    'vsi': dict(cx=722, cy=511, r0=8, r1=41),
}
HDG = dict(cx=626, cy=507, r0=14, r1=42)

NANG = 720
ANGS = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, NANG, endpoint=False)

def build_index(g):
    rs = np.arange(g['r0'], g['r1'])
    A = ANGS[:,None]; R = rs[None,:]
    xs = np.clip((g['cx'] + R*np.cos(A)).astype(int),0,1279)
    ys = np.clip((g['cy'] + R*np.sin(A)).astype(int),0,719)
    return ys, xs

IDX = {n:build_index(g) for n,g in GAUGES.items()}
HIDX = build_index(HDG)

def _circ_centroid(angs, weights):
    x=np.sum(weights*np.cos(angs)); y=np.sum(weights*np.sin(angs))
    return np.arctan2(y,x)

def needle_from_prof(prof):
    p = prof - np.median(prof)
    p[p<0]=0
    i=int(np.argmax(p)); w=8
    idx=[(i+k)%NANG for k in range(-w,w+1)]
    a=_circ_centroid(ANGS[idx], p[idx])
    return (np.degrees(a))%360, float(p.max())

def second_needle_from_prof(prof, first_deg, minsep=40):
    # zero out region around first needle then find secondary
    p = prof - np.median(prof)
    p[p<0]=0
    fi = int(round(first_deg/360.0*NANG))
    for k in range(-int(minsep/360.0*NANG), int(minsep/360.0*NANG)+1):
        p[(fi+k)%NANG]=0
    i=int(np.argmax(p)); w=8
    idx=[(i+k)%NANG for k in range(-w,w+1)]
    a=_circ_centroid(ANGS[idx], p[idx])
    return (np.degrees(a))%360, float(p.max())

def polar_card(gray):
    ys,xs=HIDX
    P = gray[ys,xs].astype(np.float32)  # (NANG, nr)
    return P

def main():
    cap=cv2.VideoCapture(VID)
    total=int(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_COUNT))
    rows=[]
    hdg_polars=[]  # store subsampled polar per record for later rotation calc
    fidx=-1
    t0=time.time()
    ref_polar=None
    # We'll compute heading rotation online vs a per-leg reference; but simpler: store all polars (downsampled) -> memory heavy.
    # Instead compute rotation vs a single global reference frame chosen at fidx of first sample.
    out=open('cv/series.csv','w')
    out.write('t,asi_ang,asi_s,alt_ang,alt_s,alt2_ang,alt2_s,vsi_ang,vsi_s\n')
    hp_all=[]
    ts=[]
    while True:
        ok=cap.grab()
        if not ok: break
        fidx+=1
        if fidx % STEP != 0: continue
        ok,frame=cap.retrieve()
        if not ok: break
        t=fidx/FPS
        gray=cv2.cvtColor(frame,cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
        rec={'t':t}
        for n in ('asi','alt','vsi'):
            ys,xs=IDX[n]
            prof=gray[ys,xs].mean(axis=1)
            d,s=needle_from_prof(prof)
            rec[n+'_ang']=d; rec[n+'_s']=s
            if n=='alt':
                d2,s2=second_needle_from_prof(prof,d)
                rec['alt2_ang']=d2; rec['alt2_s']=s2
        out.write(f"{t:.3f},{rec['asi_ang']:.2f},{rec['asi_s']:.1f},{rec['alt_ang']:.2f},{rec['alt_s']:.1f},{rec['alt2_ang']:.2f},{rec['alt2_s']:.1f},{rec['vsi_ang']:.2f},{rec['vsi_s']:.1f}\n")
        # heading polar (downsample radius mean to reduce size): store mean over radius bands
        P=polar_card(gray)  # (720, nr)
        hp_all.append(P.mean(axis=1).astype(np.float32))  # (720,)
        ts.append(t)
        if len(ts)%500==0:
            print(f"processed t={t:.1f}s frames={fidx} elapsed={time.time()-t0:.1f}s", flush=True)
    out.close()
    cap.release()
    hp=np.array(hp_all)  # (N,720)
    np.save('cv/hdg_polar.npy', hp)
    np.save('cv/hdg_t.npy', np.array(ts))
    print("done", hp.shape)

if __name__=='__main__':
    main()

I'm working through the angle convention for this coordinate system where 0° points east and positive angles rotate clockwise (since screen coordinates have y increasing downward). At t=30, the VSI reading of 180.8° points west, which correctly indicates level flight at 0 fpm.

Now I'm calibrating the ASI needle by mapping the gauge positions to angles. The needle at t=30 reads 94.5°, which points roughly downward (6 o'clock position) and corresponds to about 100 knots. I'm cross-referencing this with known values from the transcript—at t=120 there's a clearance to maintain 99 knots, and the needle positions around t=200 also suggest roughly 100 knots at similar angles. I need to establish the full ASI scale mapping from the gauge markings to get accurate speed readings throughout the flight.

At t=500 the needle jumps to 63.4° with much higher detection strength, which would place it around the 5 o'clock area corresponding to roughly 80 knots. This aligns with the clearance at t=300 to maintain 84 knots. The inconsistency in detection strength between these measurements is concerning—the low confidence at earlier timestamps makes me question whether I'm reliably tracking the needle or picking up other bright features on the gauge.

I need to build a proper calibration by identifying periods where the aircraft holds a steady target speed. The clearances give me these anchors: 99 knots held from t=120 to t=300, 84 knots from t=300 to t=540, 72 knots from t=540 to t=650, and 87 knots after t=650. I'll sample the needle angle during these stable windows to establish the angle-to-airspeed mapping.

Actually, I have something better—the flight contains roughly twenty distinct airspeed clearances ranging from 66 to 157 knots, which gives me excellent coverage across the full scale. For each clearance, I can measure the mean needle angle during the hold period and fit a linear relationship between angle and airspeed. I'll do the same for altitude calibration.

The altitude problem is trickier though—the altimeter has two needles with very different sensitivities. The long needle (hundreds) rotates 36° per 100 feet while the short needle (thousands) only rotates 3.6° per 100 feet. My detection algorithm picks whichever needle appears strongest based on pixel brightness, and the longer needle naturally has more pixels in the outer annulus, so it's likely being detected as the dominant signal.

My approach: treat the detected angle as the hundreds needle reading, which gives me a value between 0–1000 feet. Then I use the continuity of the flight path and the target altitudes from clearances to disambiguate which thousand-foot block I'm in. Since the aircraft moves smoothly between known target altitudes and I'm sampling at 2 Hz, I can track the hundreds needle continuously and unwrap the ambiguity by following the flight's trajectory.

Now I need to extract the raw time series of needle angles for the airspeed, altitude, and VSI gauges across the entire video at 2 Hz, then calibrate offline. For heading, the approach is different since it's a rotating card rather than a needle—I'll need rotational cross-correlation instead. Let me build the extraction script to pull the angle time series for those three gauges and handle heading separately.

Writing the extraction script... I can anchor the heading offset per leg by reading the card after a clearance completes—when the target heading is reached, the card top aligns with that heading, giving me the absolute reference. For the polar unwrap, I'll extract a 2D polar image from the card's informative ring (roughly 18–40 pixels radius) and cross-correlate it along the angle axis between current and reference frames to find the rotation. The rotation direction matters: on a DG, turning right increases heading but rotates the card counterclockwise so higher numbers move toward the lubber line, so I need to account for that sign flip.

+    'alt': dict(cx=723, cy=398, r0=6, r1=35),
+    'vsi': dict(cx=722, cy=511, r0=8, r1=41),
+}
+HDG = dict(cx=626, cy=507, r0=14, r1=42)
+
+NANG = 720
+ANGS = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, NANG, endpoint=False)
+
+def build_index(g):
+    rs = np.arange(g['r0'], g['r1'])
+    A = ANGS[:,None]; R = rs[None,:]
+    xs = np.clip((g['cx'] + R*np.cos(A)).astype(int),0,1279)
+    ys = np.clip((g['cy'] + R*np.sin(A)).astype(int),0,719)
+    return ys, xs
+
+IDX = {n:build_index(g) for n,g in GAUGES.items()}
+HIDX = build_index(HDG)
+

+    x=np.sum(weights*np.cos(angs)); y=np.sum(weights*np.sin(angs))

+    # zero out region around first needle then find secondary

+        p[(fi+k)%NANG]=0

+    idx=[(i+k)%NANG for k in range(-w,w+1)]

The real issues are the 'eight'/'eighty' regex bug affecting 650 and 2795, and the "nine nine" case which should be treated as digit concatenation (99) rather than word addition (18). import cv2, numpy as np

VID="materials/flight.mp4"
def avg_region(cx,cy,half,times):
    cap=cv2.VideoCapture(VID)
    acc=None; n=0
    for t in times:
        cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_MSEC,t*1000); ok,f=cap.read()
        if not ok: continue
        g=cv2.cvtColor(f,cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY).astype(np.float32)
        crop=g[cy-half:cy+half, cx-half:cx+half]
        acc=crop if acc is None else acc+crop; n+=1
    cap.release()
    return acc/n

def tick_profile(img, half, r0, r1, nang=720):
    cx=cy=half
    angs=np.linspace(0,2*np.pi,nang,endpoint=False)
    rs=np.arange(r0,r1)
    prof=np.zeros(nang)
    for i,a in enumerate(angs):
        xs=(cx+rs*np.cos(a)).astype(int); ys=(cy+rs*np.sin(a)).astype(int)
        prof[i]=img[ys,xs].mean()
    return angs,prof

if __name__=='__main__':
    import sys
    times=list(range(20,3600,7))  # spread across all legs
    # ASI
    img=avg_region(523,391,60,times)
    cv2.imwrite('cv/asi_avg.png', (img/img.max()*255).astype(np.uint8))
    ang,prof=tick_profile(img,60,30,44)
    prof=prof-prof.min()
    # find peaks
    from scipy.signal import find_peaks
    pk,_=find_peaks(np.concatenate([prof,prof[:60]]),distance=15,prominence=prof.max()*0.15)
    pk=[p%720 for p in pk if p<720]
    print("ASI tick angles(deg):", sorted(set(round(ang[p]*180/np.pi,1) for p in pk)))
    np.save('cv/asi_avgprof.npy', prof)

import cv2, numpy as np, json
VID="materials/flight.mp4"
cx,cy=723,398
NANG=720; ANGS=np.linspace(0,2*np.pi,NANG,endpoint=False)
def ann_idx(r0,r1):
    rs=np.arange(r0,r1); A=ANGS[:,None];R=rs[None,:]
    xs=np.clip((cx+R*np.cos(A)).astype(int),0,1279); ys=np.clip((cy+R*np.sin(A)).astype(int),0,719)
    return ys,xs
OUT=ann_idx(23,34)   # long hundreds needle region only
INN=ann_idx(9,20)
def peak(prof):
    p=prof-np.median(prof); p[p<0]=0
    i=int(np.argmax(p)); w=8
    idx=[(i+k)%NANG for k in range(-w,w+1)]
    x=np.sum(p[idx]*np.cos(ANGS[idx])); y=np.sum(p[idx]*np.sin(ANGS[idx]))
    return (np.degrees(np.arctan2(y,x)))%360,float(p.max())
def peak2(prof,d1,sep=45):
    p=prof-np.median(prof); p[p<0]=0
    fi=int(round(d1/360*NANG))
    for k in range(-int(sep/360*NANG),int(sep/360*NANG)+1): p[(fi+k)%NANG]=0
    i=int(np.argmax(p)); w=8
    idx=[(i+k)%NANG for k in range(-w,w+1)]
    x=np.sum(p[idx]*np.cos(ANGS[idx])); y=np.sum(p[idx]*np.sin(ANGS[idx]))
    return (np.degrees(np.arctan2(y,x)))%360,float(p.max())

def read_alt_frame(g):
    po=g[OUT[0],OUT[1]].mean(axis=1)
    hund_ang,hs=peak(po)  # hundreds needle
    pi=g[INN[0],INN[1]].mean(axis=1)
    # thousands = inner peak away from hundreds direction
    d1,_=peak(pi)
    # choose inner peak that's NOT aligned with hundreds
    a2,s2=peak2(pi,hund_ang)
    return hund_ang,hs,a2,s2

cap=cv2.VideoCapture(VID)
def frame(t):
    cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_MSEC,t*1000);ok,f=cap.read();return cv2.cvtColor(f,cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY).astype(float)
print("tgt hund  pred_h  meas_h   pred_t meas_t")

NANG=720; ANGS=np.linspace(0,2*np.pi,NANG,endpoint=False)
def ann_idx(r0,r1):
    rs=np.arange(r0,r1); A=ANGS[:,None];R=rs[None,:]
    xs=np.clip((cx+R*np.cos(A)).astype(int),0,1279); ys=np.clip((cy+R*np.sin(A)).astype(int),0,719)
    return ys,xs
OUT=ann_idx(23,34)   # long hundreds needle region only
INN=ann_idx(9,20)
def peak(prof):
    p=prof-np.median(prof); p[p<0]=0
    i=int(np.argmax(p)); w=8
    idx=[(i+k)%NANG for k in range(-w,w+1)]
    x=np.sum(p[idx]*np.cos(ANGS[idx])); y=np.sum(p[idx]*np.sin(ANGS[idx]))
    return (np.degrees(np.arctan2(y,x)))%360,float(p.max())
def peak2(prof,d1,sep=45):
    p=prof-np.median(prof); p[p<0]=0
    fi=int(round(d1/360*NANG))

    i=int(np.argmax(p)); w=8

import cv2, numpy as np
VID="materials/flight.mp4"
cx,cy=723,398
NANG=1440
ANGS=np.linspace(0,2*np.pi,NANG,endpoint=False)
COS=np.cos(ANGS); SIN=np.sin(ANGS)
RS=np.arange(5,34,0.5)
XS=np.clip((cx+RS[None,:]*COS[:,None]),0,1279).astype(int)
YS=np.clip((cy+RS[None,:]*SIN[:,None]),0,719).astype(int)
RS_out=np.arange(20,33,0.5)  # only long needle reaches here
XSo=np.clip((cx+RS_out[None,:]*COS[:,None]),0,1279).astype(int)
YSo=np.clip((cy+RS_out[None,:]*SIN[:,None]),0,719).astype(int)

def hundreds_profile(g):
    # long needle reaches outer band; weight center-anchored
    samp=g[YS,XS]
    thr=np.median(samp)+max(25,0.45*(samp.max()-np.median(samp)))
    bright=(samp>thr).astype(np.float32)
    # center-anchored run: cumulative product from center
    anchored=np.cumprod(np.maximum(bright,  # require contiguity with small tolerance
                                   0.0)+0.0, axis=1)
    # softer: contiguous run length allowing tiny gaps
    nr=samp.shape[1]
    run=np.zeros(NANG,np.float32)
    # vectorized-ish contiguous from start with gap tolerance 3
    gap=np.zeros(NANG); started=bright[:,0]>0; cur=started.astype(float)
    run=cur.copy()
    active=started.copy()
    for j in range(1,nr):
        b=bright[:,j]>0
        # start if within first few radii
        newstart=(~active)&(b)&(j<=6)
        active=active|newstart
        gap=np.where(b,0,gap+1)
        cont=active&((b)|(gap<=3))
        active=cont
        run=np.where(cont, j+1, run)
    # outer confirmation: brightness in outer band along angle
    so=g[YSo,XSo].mean(axis=1)
    so=so-np.median(so); so[so<0]=0
    score=run*so
    return score

def peak_angle(score,w=14):
    i=int(np.argmax(score))
    if score[i]<=0: return None
    idx=[(i+k)%NANG for k in range(-w,w+1)]
    x=np.sum(score[idx]*COS[idx]); y=np.sum(score[idx]*SIN[idx])
    return (np.degrees(np.arctan2(y,x)))%360

if __name__=='__main__':
    cap=cv2.VideoCapture(VID)
    def frame(t):
        cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_MSEC,t*1000);ok,f=cap.read();return cv2.cvtColor(f,cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY).astype(float)
    for t in list(range(0,20,4))+[225,300,400,485,600,700]:
        a=peak_angle(hundreds_profile(frame(t)))
        print(f"t={t} hundreds_ang={a}")

def hundreds_profile(g):
    # long needle reaches outer band; weight center-anchored
    samp=g[YS,XS]
    thr=np.median(samp)+max(25,0.45*(samp.max()-np.median(samp)))
    bright=(samp>thr).astype(np.float32)
    # center-anchored run: cumulative product from center

    # softer: contiguous run length allowing tiny gaps

    run=np.zeros(NANG,np.float32)
    # vectorized-ish contiguous from start with gap tolerance 3
    gap=np.zeros(NANG); started=bright[:,0]>0; cur=started.astype(float)

def shift(a,b):

import cv2, numpy as np
VID="materials/flight.mp4"; FPS=15.0; STEP=4
cx,cy=626,507
Y,X=np.mgrid[0:720,0:1280]
rad=np.sqrt((X-cx)**2+(Y-cy)**2)
ann=(rad>=17)&(rad<=47)
ys,xs=np.where(ann)
ang_all=(np.degrees(np.arctan2(ys-cy,xs-cx)))%360
cap=cv2.VideoCapture(VID)
ts=[]; bugang=[]; bugmass=[]
fidx=-1
while True:
    ok=cap.grab()
    if not ok: break
    fidx+=1
    if fidx%STEP: continue
    ok,f=cap.retrieve()
    if not ok: break
    f=f.astype(np.float32)
    b,g,r=f[:,:,0],f[:,:,1],f[:,:,2]
    org=(r-b)  # orange/red-ness
    vals=org[ys,xs]
    # orange also needs r>g somewhat; use r-b as main, require r> b+25
    m=vals> max(30, np.percentile(vals,99.0))
    sel=vals>30
    if sel.sum()>=3:
        w=vals[sel]-30
        aa=ang_all[sel]
        # circular weighted mean
        cxx=np.sum(w*np.cos(np.radians(aa))); cyy=np.sum(w*np.sin(np.radians(aa)))
        a=(np.degrees(np.arctan2(cyy,cxx)))%360
        mass=w.sum()
    else:
        a=np.nan; mass=0.0
    ts.append(fidx/FPS); bugang.append(a); bugmass.append(mass)
cap.release()
ts=np.array(ts); bugang=np.array(bugang); bugmass=np.array(bugmass)
np.save('cv/bug_t.npy',ts); np.save('cv/bug_ang.npy',bugang); np.save('cv/bug_mass.npy',bugmass)
print(len(ts),'median mass',np.nanmedian(bugmass))
# sanity at anchors
for t in [60,175,540,700,1050,2100,2750,3100,3595]:
    i=np.argmin(np.abs(ts-t))
    print(f"t={t} ang={bugang[i]:.1f} mass={bugmass[i]:.0f} hdg=({(252.6-bugang[i])%360:.0f})")

Looking at the trajectory data from the bug tracking, I'm noticing that frames with low mass values are producing unreliable centroid measurements—the weighted centroid gets skewed by background noise, particularly the red pixels, which throws off the position estimates compared to what I see in the eye tracking montage.

The core issue is that my orange detection threshold (r-b > 30) is too permissive and catches too much of the reddish gauge background along with the actual bug, so I'm picking up diffuse weak pixels rather than isolating the compact bright-orange blob itself. I should tighten the threshold to require both a larger r-b difference (around 60-100 for the actual bug) and positive r-g values, then find the largest connected blob and use its centroid instead.

That said, at certain timestamps the bug might genuinely be occluded or hidden, which means I should treat those as missing data and fill them through interpolation or card registration rather than forcing a measurement.

I'm considering a hybrid approach: use the bug angle as an absolute anchor when the detection is confident (high mass, compact blob), then use frame-to-frame card registration for continuity in between, possibly correcting the registration's scale error by fitting to those reliable bug anchors—though that only works if the scale error is linear. Alternatively, I could just improve the bug detection itself with stricter thresholds and connected-component analysis to require compactness, then re-examine the problematic timestamps to see if the bug is actually there or truly occluded.

Now I'm looking at the specific frames where things went wrong: at t=1050 and t=2100, the heading gauge showed around 270° (west at top), but the bug might be positioned lower in the frame, overlapping with the bezel knobs or dimmed. The real issue is that my centroid calculation used all pixels above a loose threshold, creating diffuse noise. I need to switch to a strict threshold targeting the orange color specifically—high red, moderate green, low blue—and then extract connected components to find the largest blob and compute its centroid. Let me test this refined detection at the nine anchor times with different threshold values and compare against what I can see in the montage.

I'm also compiling the ground-truth headings from the compass rose in each frame: most readings cluster around 270° (west) or 350° (north), but there's a conflict at t=3595 where the algorithm detected heading 63° while the compass clearly shows north at the top (~0-15°), suggesting the blob detection failed there despite a decent mass value.

import cv2, numpy as np, sys, time
sys.path.insert(0,'cv')
import althund as H
VID="materials/flight.mp4"; FPS=15.0; STEP=7

# ASI needle (tight annulus to avoid outer colored arc)
acx,acy=523,391
NA=720; Aang=np.linspace(0,2*np.pi,NA,endpoint=False)
Ars=np.arange(8,29)
AXS=np.clip((acx+Ars[None,:]*np.cos(Aang)[:,None]),0,1279).astype(int)
AYS=np.clip((acy+Ars[None,:]*np.sin(Aang)[:,None]),0,719).astype(int)
def asi_angle(g):
    prof=g[AYS,AXS].mean(axis=1)
    p=prof-np.median(prof); p[p<0]=0
    i=int(np.argmax(p)); w=8
    idx=[(i+k)%NA for k in range(-w,w+1)]
    x=np.sum(p[idx]*np.cos(Aang[idx])); y=np.sum(p[idx]*np.sin(Aang[idx]))
    return (np.degrees(np.arctan2(y,x)))%360

# bug
bcx,bcy=626,507
Y,X=np.mgrid[0:720,0:1280]; rad=np.sqrt((X-bcx)**2+(Y-bcy)**2)
bugmask=((rad>=17)&(rad<=47))
def bug_ang(f):
    b,g,r=f[:,:,0].astype(np.float32),f[:,:,1].astype(np.float32),f[:,:,2].astype(np.float32)
    m=((r-b>45)&(r-g>8)).astype(np.uint8); m[~bugmask]=0
    n,lab,stats,cent=cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(m)
    if n<=1: return np.nan,0
    areas=stats[1:,cv2.CC_STAT_AREA]; k=1+int(np.argmax(areas))
    a=int(areas.max())
    if a<3: return np.nan,0
    px,py=cent[k]
    return (np.degrees(np.arctan2(py-bcy,px-bcx)))%360,a

def main():
    cap=cv2.VideoCapture(VID); fidx=-1; t0=time.time()
    out=open('cv/master.csv','w'); out.write('t,asi_ang,alt_hund,bug_ang,bug_area\n')
    while True:
        ok=cap.grab()
        if not ok: break
        fidx+=1
        if fidx%STEP: continue
        ok,f=cap.retrieve()
        if not ok: break
        t=fidx/FPS
        g=cv2.cvtColor(f,cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY).astype(float)
        aa=asi_angle(g)
        ha=H.peak_angle(H.hundreds_profile(g))
        ha=ha if ha is not None else np.nan
        ba,barea=bug_ang(f)
        out.write(f"{t:.3f},{aa:.2f},{ha if np.isnan(ha) else round(ha,2)},{ba if np.isnan(ba) else round(ba,2)},{barea}\n")
        if int(t)%400==0 and fidx%STEP==0 and abs(t-round(t))<0.05:
            print(f"t={t:.0f} elapsed={time.time()-t0:.0f}s",flush=True)
    out.close(); cap.release(); print("done",time.time()-t0)

if __name__=='__main__': main()

import numpy as np, csv, json
c=np.polyfit  # noqa
# load
rows=list(csv.DictReader(open('cv/master.csv')))
t=np.array([float(r['t']) for r in rows])
def col(name):
    return np.array([np.nan if r[name] in ('nan','') else float(r[name]) for r in rows])
asi_ang=col('asi_ang'); alt_hund=col('alt_hund'); bug_ang=col('bug_ang'); bug_area=col('bug_area')
LEGS=[0,720,1440,2160,2880,3600]
def legidx(tt): 
    return np.searchsorted(LEGS,tt,side='right')-1

# ---- AIRSPEED ----
ascoef=np.load('cv/asi_cal.npy')
grid_kt=np.linspace(40,175,4001); grid_ang=np.polyval(ascoef,grid_kt)
def ang_to_kt(a): return np.interp(a,grid_ang,grid_kt)
airspeed=ang_to_kt(asi_ang)

# ---- ALTITUDE (hundreds unwrap per leg) ----
def hund_ft(a): return ((a-270)/360*1000)%1000
altrel=np.full(len(t),np.nan)
for lg in range(5):
    mask=(t>=LEGS[lg])&(t<LEGS[lg+1])
    idx=np.where(mask)[0]
    ft=hund_ft(alt_hund[idx])
    # unwrap with glitch rejection: median filter first
    out=np.array(ft)
    # forward unwrap
    for i in range(1,len(out)):
        if np.isnan(out[i]): out[i]=out[i-1]; continue
        d=out[i]-out[i-1]
        while d>500: out[i]-=1000; d=out[i]-out[i-1]
        while d<-500: out[i]+=1000; d=out[i]-out[i-1]
    altrel[idx]=out

# find stable windows per leg (variance of altrel low)
print("=== stable altitude windows per leg (relative ft) ===")
for lg in range(5):
    mask=(t>=LEGS[lg])&(t<LEGS[lg+1]); idx=np.where(mask)[0]
    a=altrel[idx]; tt=t[idx]
    # sliding std over ~20s (40 samples)
    best=None
    W=40
    for i in range(0,len(a)-W):
        seg=a[i:i+W]
        if np.nanstd(seg)<12:
            mid=tt[i+W//2]; val=np.nanmedian(seg)
            if best is None: best=(tt[i],tt[i+W], val)
    # just report first stable window found and overall
    # report a few stable windows
    ws=[]
    i=0
    while i<len(a)-W:
        seg=a[i:i+W]
        if np.nanstd(seg)<12:
            j=i
            while j<len(a)-1 and (np.isnan(a[j+1]) or abs(a[j+1]-np.nanmedian(a[i:j+2]))<20):
                j+=1
            ws.append((round(tt[i],0),round(tt[j],0),round(np.nanmedian(a[i:j]),0)))
            i=j+1
        else: i+=1
    print(f"leg{lg}:", ws[:8])

import cv2, numpy as np, sys
VID="materials/flight.mp4"
cx,cy=723,398
NANG=1440
ANGS=np.linspace(0,2*np.pi,NANG,endpoint=False)
COS=np.cos(ANGS); SIN=np.sin(ANGS)
RS=np.arange(4,34,0.5)
XS=np.clip((cx+RS[None,:]*COS[:,None]),0,1279).astype(int)
YS=np.clip((cy+RS[None,:]*SIN[:,None]),0,719).astype(int)

def needle_runs(g):
    samp=g[YS,XS]
    med=np.median(samp)
    thr=med+max(22,0.42*(samp.max()-med))
    bright=samp>thr
    nr=samp.shape[1]
    active=bright[:,0].copy(); run=active.astype(float); gap=np.zeros(NANG); maxr=np.where(active,0,-1).astype(float)
    ssum=np.where(active,samp[:,0],0.0)
    for j in range(1,nr):
        b=bright[:,j]
        newstart=(~active)&b&(j<=8); active=active|newstart
        gap=np.where(b,0,gap+1)
        cont=active&(b|(gap<=3)); active=cont
        run=np.where(cont,j+1,run)
        maxr=np.where(cont&b, j, maxr)
        ssum=np.where(cont&b, ssum+samp[:,j], ssum)
    return run, maxr, ssum

def peaks(score, k=2, sep=40):
    sc=score.copy(); res=[]
    for _ in range(k):
        i=int(np.argmax(sc))
        if sc[i]<=0: break
        w=10; idx=[(i+q)%NANG for q in range(-w,w+1)]
        x=np.sum(sc[idx]*COS[idx]); y=np.sum(sc[idx]*SIN[idx])
        ang=(np.degrees(np.arctan2(y,x)))%360
        res.append((ang,i))
        for q in range(-int(sep/360*NANG),int(sep/360*NANG)+1): sc[(i+q)%NANG]=0
    return res

def read_alt(g):
    run,maxr,ssum=needle_runs(g)
    score=run*ssum
    pk=peaks(score,2)
    if not pk: return None
    if len(pk)==1:
        # only one needle found; treat as hundreds
        a=pk[0][0]; return dict(hund=((a-270)/360*1000)%1000, thou=None, one=True, hang=a)
    (a1,i1),(a2,i2)=pk[0],pk[1]
    r1=maxr[i1]; r2=maxr[i2]
    # hundreds = longer reach
    if r1>=r2: hang,tang=a1,a2
    else: hang,tang=a2,a1
    hund=((hang-270)/360*1000)%1000
    thou=((tang-270)/360*10)%10
    return dict(hund=hund,thou=thou,hang=hang,tang=tang,r1=r1,r2=r2,one=False)

def combine(hund,thou):
    # choose N so N*1000+hund closest to thou*1000
    base=thou*1000
    N=round((base-hund)/1000.0)
    return N*1000+hund

if __name__=='__main__':
    cap=cv2.VideoCapture(VID)
    def fr(t):
        cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_MSEC,t*1000);ok,f=cap.read();return cv2.cvtColor(f,cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY).astype(float)
    tests=[8,70,113,150,225,300,485,700, 900,1100,1300, 1680,1900,2100, 2300,2550,2800, 3000,3250,3550]
    for t in tests:
        r=read_alt(fr(t))
        if r and not r['one']:
            alt=combine(r['hund'],r['thou'])
            print(f"t={t:5d} hund={r['hund']:5.0f} thou={r['thou']:.2f} r_h={r['r1'] if r['r1']>=r['r2'] else r['r2']:.0f} r_t={min(r['r1'],r['r2']):.0f} -> ALT={alt:.0f}")
        else:
            print(f"t={t} one/none {r}")

import cv2, numpy as np, sys, time
sys.path.insert(0,'cv')
import altfull as AF
VID="materials/flight.mp4"; FPS=15.0; STEP=7
cap=cv2.VideoCapture(VID); fidx=-1; t0=time.time()
out=open('cv/alt_full.csv','w'); out.write('t,hund,thou,rh,rt\n')
while True:
    ok=cap.grab()
    if not ok: break
    fidx+=1
    if fidx%STEP: continue
    ok,f=cap.retrieve()
    if not ok: break
    t=fidx/FPS
    g=cv2.cvtColor(f,cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY).astype(float)
    r=AF.read_alt(g)
    if r is None:
        out.write(f"{t:.3f},nan,nan,0,0\n"); continue
    if r['one']:
        out.write(f"{t:.3f},{r['hund']:.1f},nan,0,0\n"); continue
    rh=r['r1'] if r['r1']>=r['r2'] else r['r2']; rt=min(r['r1'],r['r2'])
    out.write(f"{t:.3f},{r['hund']:.1f},{r['thou']:.3f},{rh:.0f},{rt:.0f}\n")
    if abs(t-round(t))<0.04 and int(round(t))%600==0:
        print(f"t={t:.0f} {time.time()-t0:.0f}s",flush=True)
out.close(); cap.release(); print("done",time.time()-t0)

Either the altitude isn't 4000 or I'm misidentifying which needle is which. I'll stick with the two-needle combine as my altitude estimator but add some robustness by detecting up to three needles and assigning the hundreds value to whichever needle reaches the farthest, since that's the most reliable indicator.

For the thousands digit, I'll use temporal continuity—since it changes slowly, I can track it smoothly by taking a median over a window or using Kalman-like smoothing, anchoring it per stable flight segment. My old single-needle detector (alt_hund from the master file) locked onto the fat needle at 45° giving 376, while the correct two-needle detector (altfull) properly identifies the thin needle at 276° giving 16. I need to rebuild the altitude pipeline using altfull's two-needle reader across the entire video at 2Hz, extracting hundreds, thousands, and combined altitude values. import numpy as np, csv, sys, json
sys.path.insert(0,'cv'); import altfull as AF
from scipy.ndimage import median_filter

LEGS=[0,720,1440,2160,2880,3600]

# ---------- load ----------
ar=list(csv.DictReader(open('cv/alt_full.csv')))
t=np.array([float(r['t']) for r in ar])
def fcol(rows,name):
    return np.array([np.nan if rows[i][name] in ('nan','') else float(rows[i][name]) for i in range(len(rows))])
hund=fcol(ar,'hund'); thou=fcol(ar,'thou'); rh=fcol(ar,'rh'); rt=fcol(ar,'rt')

mr=list(csv.DictReader(open('cv/master.csv')))
tm=np.array([float(r['t']) for r in mr])
asi_ang=np.array([float(r['asi_ang']) for r in mr])

bt=np.load('cv/bug_t.npy'); bang=np.load('cv/bug_ang.npy'); barea=np.load('cv/bug_mass.npy')  # mass placeholder
# recompute bug via area file if exists
try:
    barea=np.load('cv/bug_area.npy')
except: pass

N=len(t)
# ---------- AIRSPEED ----------
ascoef=np.load('cv/asi_cal.npy')
gk=np.linspace(40,175,4001); ga=np.polyval(ascoef,gk)
asi_kt=np.interp(asi_ang, ga, gk)
# align to alt timestamps (same STEP so identical) -- both 2Hz same frames
airspeed=median_filter(asi_kt,size=5)

# ---------- ALTITUDE ----------
def hund_ft_of(a): return ((a-270)/360*1000)%1000
altitude=np.full(N,np.nan)
comb=np.array([AF.combine(h,tv) if not(np.isnan(h) or np.isnan(tv)) else np.nan for h,tv in zip(hund,thou)])
for lg in range(5):
    idx=np.where((t>=LEGS[lg])&(t<LEGS[lg+1]))[0]
    hf=hund_ft_of(hund[idx])
    hf=median_filter(hf,size=3)
    # unwrap
    uw=np.array(hf,float)
    for i in range(1,len(uw)):
        d=uw[i]-uw[i-1]
        while d>500: uw[i]-=1000; d=uw[i]-uw[i-1]
        while d<-500: uw[i]+=1000; d=uw[i]-uw[i-1]
    # trustworthy combine frames: needles separated & rt reasonable
    cf=comb[idx]
    sep=np.abs(((hund[idx]-(hund[idx]))))  # placeholder
    trust=(rt[idx]>=10)&(rt[idx]<=42)&(rh[idx]>=35)&(~np.isnan(cf))
    off_samples=cf[trust]-uw[trust]
    if len(off_samples)>0:
        C=np.round(np.median(off_samples)/1000.0)*1000
    else:
        C=np.round(np.nanmedian(cf-uw)/1000.0)*1000
    altitude[idx]=uw+C
altitude=median_filter(altitude,size=3)

# ---------- HEADING ----------
K=612.6
hdg_raw=(K-bang)%360
good=(barea>=10)&(~np.isnan(bang))
# build on alt timestamps t via nearest bug sample; but bug has own STEP=4. interpolate.
# unwrap good headings over time then interp
heading=np.full(N,np.nan)
# process per leg to avoid cross-boundary unwrap
for lg in range(5):
    bm=(bt>=LEGS[lg])&(bt<LEGS[lg+1])&good
    bts=bt[bm]; bhs=hdg_raw[bm]
    if len(bts)<2:
        continue
    # unwrap
    uh=np.unwrap(np.radians(bhs)); uh=np.degrees(uh)
    # interp onto t within leg
    im=(t>=LEGS[lg])&(t<LEGS[lg+1])
    heading[im]=np.interp(t[im], bts, uh)
heading=heading%360

np.savez('cv/series_clean.npz', t=t, altitude=altitude, airspeed=airspeed, heading=heading, comb=comb, hund=hund, thou=thou)
# sanity print
print("leg offsets & sample altitudes:")
for lg in range(5):
    idx=np.where((t>=LEGS[lg])&(t<LEGS[lg+1]))[0]
    print(f" leg{lg}: alt range {np.nanmin(altitude[idx]):.0f}..{np.nanmax(altitude[idx]):.0f}")
for tt in [8,150,300,500,700,900,1200,1500,1700,2000,2300,2600,2900,3100,3400,3590]:
    i=np.argmin(np.abs(t-tt))
    print(f"  t={tt:5d} alt={altitude[i]:6.0f} spd={airspeed[i]:5.1f} hdg={heading[i]:5.1f}")

import numpy as np, csv, sys
sys.path.insert(0,'cv'); import altfull as AF
from scipy.ndimage import median_filter
LEGS=[0,720,1440,2160,2880,3600]
ar=list(csv.DictReader(open('cv/alt_full.csv')))
t=np.array([float(r['t']) for r in ar])
hund=np.array([np.nan if r['hund']=='nan' else float(r['hund']) for r in ar])
thou=np.array([np.nan if r['thou']=='nan' else float(r['thou']) for r in ar])
rh=np.array([float(r['rh']) for r in ar]); rt=np.array([float(r['rt']) for r in ar])
comb=np.array([AF.combine(h,tv) if not(np.isnan(h) or np.isnan(tv)) else np.nan for h,tv in zip(hund,thou)])

def unwrap_leg(hf):
    hf=median_filter(hf,size=5)
    uw=np.array(hf,float)
    for i in range(1,len(uw)):
        d=uw[i]-uw[i-1]
        while d>500: uw[i]-=1000; d=uw[i]-uw[i-1]
        while d<-500: uw[i]+=1000; d=uw[i]-uw[i-1]
    # deglitch: remove short spikes via second median on unwrapped
    uw2=median_filter(uw,size=7)
    return uw2

# leg0 test, anchor at t=150 -> 4016 (eye verified 4000)
lg=0
idx=np.where((t>=LEGS[lg])&(t<LEGS[lg+1]))[0]
uw=unwrap_leg(((hund[idx]-270)/360*1000)%1000)
# anchor: find sample near t=150
ai=np.argmin(np.abs(t[idx]-150)); C=4016-uw[ai]
alt=uw+C
for tt in range(0,720,30):
    j=np.argmin(np.abs(t[idx]-tt))
    print(f"t={tt:4d} alt={alt[j]:6.0f}  (comb={comb[idx][j]:.0f})")

import numpy as np, csv, sys
sys.path.insert(0,'cv'); import altfull as AF
from scipy.ndimage import median_filter
LEGS=[0,720,1440,2160,2880,3600]
ar=list(csv.DictReader(open('cv/alt_full.csv')))
t=np.array([float(r['t']) for r in ar])
hund=np.array([np.nan if r['hund']=='nan' else float(r['hund']) for r in ar])
thou=np.array([np.nan if r['thou']=='nan' else float(r['thou']) for r in ar])
comb=np.array([AF.combine(h,tv) if not(np.isnan(h) or np.isnan(tv)) else np.nan for h,tv in zip(hund,thou)])

def solve_leg(idx):
    hf=((hund[idx]-270)/360*1000)%1000
    hf=median_filter(hf,size=5)
    cf=median_filter(comb[idx],size=9)
    n=len(idx)
    # initial kilofoot from robust median of cf in first 30 stable samples
    # running estimate
    alt=np.full(n,np.nan)
    # seed: use median combine of a stable early window
    seed=np.nanmedian(cf[:60]) if n>=60 else np.nanmedian(cf)
    pred=seed
    for i in range(n):
        h=hf[i]
        # candidate altitudes with this hundreds digit near pred
        base=round((pred-h)/1000.0)
        cands=[(base+k)*1000+h for k in (-1,0,1)]
        a=min(cands,key=lambda x:abs(x-pred))
        alt[i]=a
        pred=0.6*pred+0.4*a  # smooth predictor
    # final light smoothing
    alt=median_filter(alt,size=5)
    return alt

alt=np.full(len(t),np.nan)
for lg in range(5):
    idx=np.where((t>=LEGS[lg])&(t<LEGS[lg+1]))[0]
    alt[idx]=solve_leg(idx)
np.save('cv/altitude_series.npy', alt); np.save('cv/alt_t.npy', t)
for tt in range(0,3600,90):
    i=np.argmin(np.abs(t-tt)); print(f"t={tt:4d} alt={alt[i]:6.0f} comb={comb[i] if not np.isnan(comb[i]) else -1:.0f}")

import numpy as np, csv, sys
sys.path.insert(0,'cv'); import altfull as AF
from scipy.ndimage import median_filter
LEGS=[0,720,1440,2160,2880,3600]

ar=list(csv.DictReader(open('cv/alt_full.csv')))
t=np.array([float(r['t']) for r in ar])
hund=np.array([np.nan if r['hund']=='nan' else float(r['hund']) for r in ar])
thou=np.array([np.nan if r['thou']=='nan' else float(r['thou']) for r in ar])
comb=np.array([AF.combine(h,tv) if not(np.isnan(h) or np.isnan(tv)) else np.nan for h,tv in zip(hund,thou)])

# airspeed
mr=list(csv.DictReader(open('cv/master.csv')))
asi_ang=np.array([float(r['asi_ang']) for r in mr])
ascoef=np.load('cv/asi_cal.npy'); gk=np.linspace(40,175,4001); ga=np.polyval(ascoef,gk)
airspeed=np.interp(asi_ang,ga,gk)
airspeed=median_filter(airspeed,size=5)

# altitude: robust per-leg kilofoot via majority vote in sliding window, hundreds reliable
def hf_of(a): return ((a-270)/360*1000)%1000
altitude=np.full(len(t),np.nan)
for lg in range(5):
    idx=np.where((t>=LEGS[lg])&(t<LEGS[lg+1]))[0]
    hf=median_filter(hf_of(hund[idx]),size=5)
    c=comb[idx]
    N=np.round((c-hf)/1000.0)
    # robust: median filter N heavily to get stable kilofoot
    Nf=median_filter(np.nan_to_num(N,nan=np.nanmedian(N)),size=21)
    Nf=np.round(Nf)
    a=Nf*1000+hf
    a=median_filter(a,size=5)
    altitude[idx]=a

# heading from bug
bt=np.load('cv/bug_t.npy'); bang=np.load('cv/bug_ang.npy'); barea=np.load('cv/bug_area.npy')
K=612.6
hraw=(K-bang)%360
good=(barea>=10)&(~np.isnan(bang))
heading=np.full(len(t),np.nan)
for lg in range(5):
    bm=(bt>=LEGS[lg])&(bt<LEGS[lg+1])&good
    bts=bt[bm]; bhs=hraw[bm]
    if len(bts)<2: continue
    uh=np.degrees(np.unwrap(np.radians(bhs)))
    # despike bug: median filter unwrapped
    uh=median_filter(uh,size=5)
    im=(t>=LEGS[lg])&(t<LEGS[lg+1])
    heading[im]=np.interp(t[im],bts,uh)
heading=heading%360

np.savez('cv/final_series.npz', t=t, altitude=altitude, airspeed=airspeed, heading=heading)
print("saved. spot values:")
for tt in [8,150,300,500,700,900,1100,1300,1500,1700,1900,2100,2300,2500,2700,2900,3100,3300,3500,3590]:
    i=np.argmin(np.abs(t-tt))
    print(f" t={tt:5d} alt={altitude[i]:6.0f} spd={airspeed[i]:5.1f} hdg={heading[i]:5.1f}")

import numpy as np, csv, sys
sys.path.insert(0,'cv'); import altfull as AF
from scipy.ndimage import median_filter
LEGS=[0,720,1440,2160,2880,3600]

ar=list(csv.DictReader(open('cv/alt_full.csv')))
t=np.array([float(r['t']) for r in ar])
hund=np.array([np.nan if r['hund']=='nan' else float(r['hund']) for r in ar])
thou=np.array([np.nan if r['thou']=='nan' else float(r['thou']) for r in ar])
comb=np.array([AF.combine(h,tv) if not(np.isnan(h) or np.isnan(tv)) else np.nan for h,tv in zip(hund,thou)])

# airspeed
mr=list(csv.DictReader(open('cv/master.csv')))
asi_ang=np.array([float(r['asi_ang']) for r in mr])
ascoef=np.load('cv/asi_cal.npy'); gk=np.linspace(40,175,4001); ga=np.polyval(ascoef,gk)
airspeed=np.interp(asi_ang,ga,gk)
airspeed=median_filter(airspeed,size=5)

# altitude: robust per-leg kilofoot via majority vote in sliding window, hundreds reliable
def hf_of(a): return ((a-270)/360*1000)%1000
altitude=np.full(len(t),np.nan)
for lg in range(5):
    idx=np.where((t>=LEGS[lg])&(t<LEGS[lg+1]))[0]
    hf=median_filter(hf_of(hund[idx]),size=5)
    c=comb[idx]
    N=np.round((c-hf)/1000.0)
    # robust: median filter N heavily to get stable kilofoot
    Nf=median_filter(np.nan_to_num(N,nan=np.nanmedian(N)),size=21)
    Nf=np.round(Nf)
    a=Nf*1000+hf
    a=median_filter(a,size=5)
    altitude[idx]=a

# heading from bug
bt=np.load('cv/bug_t.npy'); bang=np.load('cv/bug_ang.npy'); barea=np.load('cv/bug_area.npy')
K=612.6
hraw=(K-bang)%360
good=(barea>=10)&(~np.isnan(bang))
heading=np.full(len(t),np.nan)
for lg in range(5):
    bm=(bt>=LEGS[lg])&(bt<LEGS[lg+1])&good
    bts=bt[bm]; bhs=hraw[bm]
    if len(bts)<2: continue
    uh=np.degrees(np.unwrap(np.radians(bhs)))
    # despike bug: median filter unwrapped
    uh=median_filter(uh,size=5)
    im=(t>=LEGS[lg])&(t<LEGS[lg+1])
    heading[im]=np.interp(t[im],bts,uh)
heading=heading%360

np.savez('cv/final_series.npz', t=t, altitude=altitude, airspeed=airspeed, heading=heading)
print("saved. spot values:")
for tt in [8,150,300,500,700,900,1100,1300,1500,1700,1900,2100,2300,2500,2700,2900,3100,3300,3500,3590]:
    i=np.argmin(np.abs(t-tt))
    print(f" t={tt:5d} alt={altitude[i]:6.0f} spd={airspeed[i]:5.1f} hdg={heading[i]:5.1f}")

--- a/dev/null
+++ b/workspace/cv/events.py
@@ -1,0 +1,176 @@
+import numpy as np, json
+d=np.load('cv/final_series.npz')
+t=d['t']; ALT=d['altitude']; SPD=d['airspeed']; HDG=d['heading']
+cls=json.load(open('cv/clearances_parsed.json'))
+LEGS=[0,720,1440,2160,2880,3600]
+def leg_of(tt):
+    for i in range(5):
+        if LEGS[i]<=tt<LEGS[i+1]: return i
+    return 4
+for c in cls: c['leg']=leg_of(c['t'])
+
+DIMSERIES={'alt':ALT,'hdg':HDG,'spd':SPD}
+TOL={'alt':100,'hdg':8,'spd':3}          # completion tolerance
+STATETOL={'alt':25,'hdg':2,'spd':2}
+EXTHR={'alt':1.6667,'hdg':0.5,'spd':0.5} # per-second execution thresholds
+UNIT={'alt':'feet','hdg':'degrees','spd':'knots'}
+
+def sample(series,tt):
+    i=int(np.argmin(np.abs(t-tt)))
+    return float(series[i])
+def state_at(tt):
+    return dict(alt=round(sample(ALT,tt)), hdg=round(sample(HDG,tt))%360, spd=round(sample(SPD,tt)))
+
+def circ_signed(a,b):  # signed shortest a-b in (-180,180]
+    x=(a-b)%360
+    if x>180: x-=360
+    return x
+
+# direction sign per command
+def commanded_dir(c):
+    return {'climb':+1,'descend':-1,'accelerate':+1,'decelerate':-1,
+            'turn_right_heading':+1,'turn_left_heading':-1}[c['cmd_final']]
+
+# finalize cmd type for speed
+def finalize(cls):
+    for c in cls:
+        if c['dim']=='spd':
+            # need pre-clearance airspeed
+            pre=sample(SPD,c['t']-1)
+            c['cmd_final']='accelerate' if pre< c['target'] else 'decelerate'
+        elif c['dim']=='alt':
+            c['cmd_final']=c['cmd']  # climb/descend
+        else:
+            c['cmd_final']=c['cmd']  # turn_left_heading/right
+finalize(cls)
+
+def win_end(c):
+    leg=c['leg']; nxt=None
+    for c2 in cls:
+        if c2['dim']==c['dim'] and c2['leg']==leg and c2['t']>c['t']:
+            nxt=c2; break
+    return (nxt['t'] if nxt else LEGS[leg+1]), nxt
+
+def series_window(series,t0,t1):
+    m=(t>=t0)&(t<=t1)
+    return t[m], series[m]
+
+def progress_and_overshoot(c, issue_val):
+    series=DIMSERIES[c['dim']]; we,_=win_end(c)
+    tw,vw=series_window(series,c['t'],we)
+    if len(vw)==0: return 0.0,'none'
+    dirn=commanded_dir(c); T=c['target']
+    if c['dim']=='hdg':
+        prog=np.array([circ_signed(v,issue_val)*dirn for v in vw])  # progress in commanded dir
+        maxprog=max(0.0,float(np.max(prog)))
+        tgt_dist=(circ_signed(T,issue_val)*dirn)%360
+        if tgt_dist>180: tgt_dist-=360
+        # target distance in commanded direction (0..360 measured in dir)
+        tgt_dist=( (T-issue_val)%360 ) if dirn>0 else ((issue_val-T)%360)
+        exc=maxprog-tgt_dist
+        bucket= 'large' if exc>15 else ('small' if exc>8 else 'none')
+        return round(maxprog,1),bucket
+    else:
+        vals=vw*dirn
+        maxr=float(np.max(vals)); base=issue_val*dirn
+        maxprog=max(0.0,maxr-base)
+        exc=maxr-(T*dirn)
+        if c['dim']=='alt':
+            bucket='large' if exc>250 else ('small' if exc>100 else 'none')
+        else:
+            bucket='large' if exc>10 else ('small' if exc>3 else 'none')
+        return round(maxprog,1),bucket
+
+def slope_dir(series,ti,dur=2.0):
+    m=(t>=ti)&(t<=ti+dur)
+    if m.sum()<3: return None
+    tt=t[m]; vv=series[m]
+    if series is HDG:
+        vv=np.unwrap(np.radians(vv)); vv=np.degrees(vv)
+    A=np.polyfit(tt-tt[0],vv,1)
+    return A[0]  # per second
+
+def execution_start(c):
+    series=DIMSERIES[c['dim']]; we,_=win_end(c)
+    dirn=commanded_dir(c); thr=EXTHR[c['dim']]
+    idx=np.where((t>c['t'])&(t<=we-2))[0]
+    for i in idx:
+        s=slope_dir(series,t[i])
+        if s is None: continue
+        if s*dirn>=thr:
+            return float(t[i])
+    return None
+
+def wrongdir_trend(c):
+    series=DIMSERIES[c['dim']]; we,_=win_end(c)
+    dirn=commanded_dir(c); thr=EXTHR[c['dim']]
+    idx=np.where((t>c['t'])&(t<=we-2))[0]
+    for i in idx:
+        s=slope_dir(series,t[i])
+        if s is None: continue
+        if s*(-dirn)>=thr:
+            return True
+    return False
+
+def completion_time(c, exec_t):
+    if exec_t is None: return None
+    series=DIMSERIES[c['dim']]; we,_=win_end(c); T=c['target']; tol=TOL[c['dim']]
+    idx=np.where((t>=exec_t)&(t<=we-3))[0]
+    for i in idx:
+        m=(t>=t[i])&(t<=we)
+        vv=series[m]
+        if c['dim']=='hdg':
+            dev=np.abs([circ_signed(v,T) for v in vv])
+        else:
+            dev=np.abs(vv-T)
+        if np.all(dev<=tol):
+            return float(t[i])
+    return None
+
+out=[]
+for i,c in enumerate(cls):
+    issue=state_at(c['t'])
+    issue_val={'alt':issue['alt'],'hdg':issue['hdg'],'spd':issue['spd']}[c['dim']]
+    we,nxt=win_end(c)
+    maxprog,bucket=progress_and_overshoot(c,issue_val)
+    exec_t=execution_start(c)
+    comp_t=completion_time(c,exec_t)
+    # status
+    if comp_t is not None:
+        status='complied_late' if (exec_t-c['t'])>12 else 'complied'
+        superseded_by=None
+    elif nxt is not None:
+        status='superseded'; superseded_by=cls.index(nxt)+1
+    elif wrongdir_trend(c):
+        status='violated'; superseded_by=None
+    else:
+        status='incomplete'; superseded_by=None
+    exs=state_at(exec_t) if exec_t is not None else dict(alt=None,hdg=None,spd=None)
+    cos=state_at(comp_t) if comp_t is not None else dict(alt=None,hdg=None,spd=None)
+    ends=state_at(min(we-0.3, LEGS[c['leg']+1]-0.3))
+    rec={
+      'clearance_index':i+1,
+      'issued_time_s':round(c['t'],1),
+      'command_type':c['cmd_final'],
+      'target_value':c['target'],
+      'target_unit':UNIT[c['dim']],
+      'issue_altitude_ft':issue['alt'],'issue_heading_deg':issue['hdg'],'issue_airspeed_kt':issue['spd'],
+      'maximum_commanded_progress':maxprog,
+      'execution_altitude_ft':exs['alt'],'execution_heading_deg':exs['hdg'],'execution_airspeed_kt':exs['spd'],
+      'completion_altitude_ft':cos['alt'],'completion_heading_deg':cos['hdg'],'completion_airspeed_kt':cos['spd'],
+      'ending_altitude_ft':ends['alt'],'ending_heading_deg':ends['hdg'],'ending_airspeed_kt':ends['spd'],
+      'execution_start_time_s':round(exec_t,1) if exec_t is not None else None,
+      'completion_time_s':round(comp_t,1) if comp_t is not None else None,
+      'status':status,
+      'superseded_by_index':superseded_by,
+      'overshoot_bucket':bucket,
+    }
+    out.append(rec)
+
+json.dump({'clearances':out}, open('cv/solution_draft.json','w'), indent=2)
+# print summary
+for r in out:
+    print(r['clearance_index'],r['command_type'],'tgt',r['target_value'],'| iss a%d h%d s%d'%(r['issue_altitude_ft'],r['issue_heading_deg'],r['issue_airspeed_kt']),
+          '| prog',r['maximum_commanded_progress'],'| exec',r['execution_start_time_s'],'comp',r['completion_time_s'],'|',r['status'],'ovr',r['overshoot_bucket'])
+from collections import Counter
+print(Counter(r['status'] for r in out))

# altitude: hundreds digit reliable; kilofoot via Viterbi smoothing of combine votes
def hf_of(a): return ((a-270)/360*1000)%1000
altitude=np.full(len(t),np.nan)
NMAX=6; LAM=7.0
for lg in range(5):
    idx=np.where((t>=LEGS[lg])&(t<LEGS[lg+1]))[0]
    hf=median_filter(hf_of(hund[idx]),size=5)
    c=comb[idx]
    Nvote=np.round((c-hf)/1000.0)
    n=len(idx)
    # DP
    INF=1e9
    dp=np.full((n,NMAX+1),INF); bk=np.zeros((n,NMAX+1),int)
    for N in range(NMAX+1):
        dp[0,N]=0 if (not np.isnan(Nvote[0]) and N==Nvote[0]) else (0.3 if np.isnan(Nvote[0]) else 1.0)
    for i in range(1,n):
        emit=np.array([0 if (not np.isnan(Nvote[i]) and N==Nvote[i]) else (0.3 if np.isnan(Nvote[i]) else 1.0) for N in range(NMAX+1)])
        for N in range(NMAX+1):
            costs=dp[i-1]+LAM*np.abs(np.arange(NMAX+1)-N)
            j=int(np.argmin(costs)); dp[i,N]=costs[j]+emit[N]; bk[i,N]=j
    N=int(np.argmin(dp[-1])); path=[N]
    for i in range(n-1,0,-1):
        N=bk[i,N]; path.append(N)
    path=np.array(path[::-1])
    altitude[idx]=path*1000+hf
altitude=median_filter(altitude,size=3)

        c=np.interp(np.arange(len(c)), np.where(ok)[0], c[ok])

The real culprit is that huge progress values like 2581, 3902, 4256, and 4724 kilofoot are artifacts of altitude glitches surviving the median filter during kilofoot ambiguity periods. These false jumps are throwing off the maximum commanded progress calculation and causing overshoot detection to misfire. The airspeed values look reasonable, but the altitude series is the weak point dragging down the overall quality of the solution.

I'm considering whether to invest more time in fixing this. The structure, timing, targets, command types, headings, and airspeeds are solid, but the altitude kilofoot errors are creating cascading problems. I could try a stronger de-glitching approach with rate limiting, but the plane does make legitimate large altitude changes so I can't be too aggressive. A more robust fix would be to use global optimization across each leg to determine the kilofoot sequence that minimizes total variation while respecting the reliable hundreds digits, but that's getting complex.

For now, I'm leaning toward a simpler targeted approach: apply a median filter to smooth the kilofoot values derived from the combine votes within each leg, then reconstruct the full altitude. For each frame, I'll compute a cost based on how far the current kilofoot value is from what the combine votes suggest, plus a transition penalty for switching between kilofoot levels. This finds the minimum-cost path through the kilofoot states (0 through 6), which smooths out brief glitches while allowing real altitude changes. A glitch persisting for k frames costs less to remove if k is smaller than the transition penalty, so with LAMBDA=6, glitches under 12 frames get filtered out while real changes lasting 30-120 seconds survive. Now I'm implementing the Viterbi algorithm to find the optimal kilofoot sequence per leg, relying on the reliable hundred-foot measurements and combine data.

## Approach

**Audio → clearances:** Ran `./transcribe` over the full 60‑minute recording, parsed 65 timestamped clearances across the 5 legs. Fixed word→number bugs (`nine nine`→99, `eighty seven`→87). Speed commands classified as accelerate/decelerate vs. the pre‑clearance airspeed.

**Video → instrument state** (built a CV pipeline in `cv/`, sampled at 2 Hz over all 3600 s):
- **Airspeed** — needle‑angle detection on the ASI, calibrated with a quadratic fit against speed‑hold windows (residuals < 0.6 kt).
- **Altitude** — dual‑needle altimeter read per frame: the longer (hundreds) needle for the precise last‑3 digits + the shorter (thousands) needle for the kilofoot, combined and kilofoot‑smoothed with a Viterbi pass. Verified by eye at multiple holds (e.g. t=150≈4016, t=500≈1356).
- **Heading** — the rotating compass card is read via the orange card‑fixed bug (self‑calibrated: heading = (612.6 − bug_angle) mod 360, consistent to ±1°).

**Event logic:** Per clearance I computed issue/execution/completion/ending states, `maximum_commanded_progress` (circular for heading), execution‑start (sustained correct‑direction trend), completion (stable within tolerance to window end), status precedence (complied → superseded → violated → incomplete), supersession links, and overshoot buckets.

## Result
33 superseded, 17 complied, 7 incomplete, 7 violated, 1 complied_late — consistent with an aircraft that frequently receives new same‑dimension clearances before completing prior ones and often does not fully track commanded targets.

Note: transcript‑derived fields (times, command types, targets), airspeed, and heading are high‑confidence; altitude is accurate at stable holds but the dim dual‑needle altimeter leaves some kilofoot ambiguity in fast transitions and a few leg‑1 windows.
